title: Review of c16's Swarm Chemistry 3/18 negative: replicated on fresh seed 7 (64 splits, 1 persistent, 67 merges; blue share 0.24 in cores, 0.47 at the edge); labkit on the same recipe: 0 persistent splits, merge/split 0.83
summary: Ran c16's body18.py unchanged on fresh seed 7 (1200 agents, 1400^2 box, 3000 steps) and a labkit pack of the same recipe 3/18 through the sighting's world.py (recipe, N and box passed by WORLD_P, wp.json; the only edit in world_3species.py is a 3-entry channel list, because the world's 2-name list made labkit crash at the timeseries plot for 3 species). body18: 1-5 bodies (mean 1.9), 64 splits, 1 persistent at 400 steps, 67 merges; the long-range blue species rises from 0.20-0.24 of agents in the core to 0.47 at the edge while red and green fall from ~0.35-0.44 to 0.24-0.29. labkit (density grid): 350 splits, 0 persistent, merge/split 0.83; particles.png shows one to three large blue-coated bodies that pinch apart and fuse again throughout the run.

observations.negative: b18_s7.json: splits 64, persistent_splits_400 1, merges 67; rerun/seed7/particles.png: bodies re-fuse; blue edge share 0.47 vs 0.20-0.24 in cores

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. labkit's grid segmentation of a particle density is noisy for this world (612 nucleations, longest track 5 frames), so its counts are only a cross-check; body18's agent-overlap tracking is the better measure.
